title: Towards Reproducibility in Predictive Process Mining: SPICE -- A Deep Learning Library
abstract: arXiv:2512.16715v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: In recent years, Predictive Process Mining (PPM) techniques based on artificial neural networks have evolved as a method for monitoring the future behavior of unfolding business processes and predicting Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). However, many PPM approaches often lack reproducibility, transparency in decision making, usability for incorporating novel datasets and benchmarking, making comparisons among different implementations very difficult. In this paper, we propose SPICE, a Python framework that reimplements three popular, existing baseline deep-learning-based methods for PPM in PyTorch, while designing a common base framework with rigorous configurability to enable reproducible and robust comparison of past and future modelling approaches. We compare SPICE to original reported metrics and with fair metrics on 11 datasets.

translated_title: 迈向预测性流程挖掘的可复现性：SPICE——一个深度学习库
translated_abstract: 摘要：近年来，基于人工神经网络的预测性流程挖掘（PPM）技术已发展为一种监测正在展开的业务流程未来行为并预测关键绩效指标（KPI）的方法。然而，许多PPM方法往往缺乏可复现性、决策透明度、对整合新数据集和基准测试的易用性，这使得不同实现之间的比较变得非常困难。在本文中，我们提出了SPICE，一个Python框架，它用PyTorch重新实现了三种流行的现有基于深度学习的PPM基线方法，同时设计了一个具有严格可配置性的通用基础框架，以实现对过去和未来建模方法的可复现且稳健的比较。我们将SPICE与原始报告指标以及在11个数据集上使用公平指标进行比较。
tldr: 本文提出SPICE，一个基于PyTorch的Python框架，通过可配置的通用基础框架重新实现三种深度学习PPM基线方法，以提升可复现性并支持跨数据集的公平比较。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SPICE, a PyTorch-based Python framework that reimplements three deep-learning PPM baselines with a configurable common base to enhance reproducibility and enable fair comparisons across 11 datasets.
